claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding undergo rapid Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
A 50–100 nm Al interlayer between the Zr-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating is an optimized thickness range.
A nanoscale metallic interlayer can be deposited by a physical-vapor-deposition method.
Controlled thermal pretreatment of the Cr/Al/Zr stack will promote formation of an intermetallic diffusion barrier.
Initial thermal exposure will cause the Al interlayer to form controlled, coherent Cr2Al and/or Al–Zr compounds at the interfaces.
The proposed Cr2Al and/or Al–Zr intermetallic layer will be stable and coherent under the stated exposures.
The intermetallic barrier will increase the activation energy for Cr and Zr interdiffusion.
Increasing the activation energy for Cr–Zr interdiffusion will reduce Cr and Zr diffusive flux at elevated temperature.
The Al-derived barrier will significantly reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion relative to a directly deposited Cr coating.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prolong coating integrity.
The Al interlayer will not compromise the protective function of the outer Cr layer.
The modified coating will maintain protective oxide formation in approximately 320 °C pressurized water.
The modified coating will maintain protective oxide formation in steam at temperatures up to approximately 1200 °C for up to one hour.
Approximately 320 °C pressurized water represents the normal-operation boundary for evaluating the intervention.
Approximately 1200 °C steam for up to one hour represents the accident-exposure boundary for evaluating the intervention.
Al is relevant to the design of accident-tolerant cladding for high-temperature steam oxidation.
Mechanical brittleness or loss of integrity of the intermetallic layer could compromise coating performance.
Failure to reduce interdiffusion, or degradation of adhesion or fracture toughness relative to the direct-Cr baseline, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The direct-Cr baseline contains no Al layer or Cr/Al/Zr interfaces, yet falsification is framed in terms of comparing the Al-containing intermetallic-layer thickness at Cr/Al/Zr interfaces with the baseline. The comparable baseline quantity is therefore not consistently defined.
